data.title: Notoginsenoside R1 Alleviates Acetaminophen-Induced Liver Injury via MAPK/mTOR-Mediated Autophagy.
data.authors: Li S; Liu Z; Pan G; Li S; Lv G; Tang S; Li J; Li Q; Wu M; Yuan G; Yu S; Ouyang G
data.journal: The American Journal of Chinese Medicine

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Notoginsenoside R1 alleviates acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury by activating protective autophagy through MAPK/mTOR pathway modulation, reducing hepatocyte death and oxidative damage.
data.abstract_excerpt: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is a leading cause of acute liver injury (ALI), yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. Although notoginsenoside R1 (NGR1) is a major bioactive saponin isolated from Panax notoginseng with established anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant properties, its hepatoprotective potential and underlying mechanisms in APAP-induced liver injury (AILI) have not been systematically investigated.

extracted_findings.effect: NGR1 suppresses mTOR to activate autophagy, reducing APAP-induced hepatocyte apoptosis and liver injury

extracted_findings_review.note: AI-assisted extraction from the paper. The curated finding takes precedence where the two disagree.
